wordDescription: This problem concerns the asymptotic behavior of the number of iterations required by the Conjugate Gradient (CG) method versus the Randomized Chebyshev Descent (RCD) method when applied to a random positive definite linear system with a specific eigenvalue distribution. The matrix is constructed as a Haar unitary conjugation of a diagonal matrix with eigenvalues decaying polynomially as $k^{-p}$. The right-hand side is generated by applying this matrix to a uniformly random unit vector. The question asks how the iteration counts $T_{\rm CG}$ and $T_{\rm RCD}$ compare as the dimension $n$ grows, for fixed tolerance $\varepsilon$ and decay exponent $p$. This is important because it probes the efficiency of deterministic Krylov methods versus randomized polynomial methods under a challenging spectral distribution that mimics ill-conditioned problems with clustered eigenvalues. Understanding this asymptotic comparison can inform algorithm selection in large-scale numerical linear algebra, especially for problems where the spectrum has a power-law decay.
mathematicalConditions: Let $\mathbf{A}_n = \mathbf{U} \operatorname{diag}(1^{-p}, \dots, n^{-p}) \mathbf{U}^*$ with $\mathbf{U}$ Haar unitary and $\mathbf{b}_n = \mathbf{A}_n \mathbf{z}_n$ where $\mathbf{z}_n$ is uniform on the unit sphere. Define $T_{\rm CG}(\mathbf{A}_n, \mathbf{b}_n, \varepsilon)$ as the minimal number of CG iterations to achieve relative residual norm $\le \varepsilon$ (in some norm), and similarly $T_{\rm RCD}$. The problem asks for the asymptotic ratio or difference $T_{\rm CG}/T_{\rm RCD}$ or $T_{\rm CG} - T_{\rm RCD}$ as $n \to \infty$. Progress would be a rigorous characterization of these quantities, e.g., showing that $T_{\rm CG} \sim c_1 n^{1/(2p)}$ and $T_{\rm RCD} \sim c_2 n^{1/(2p)}$ with explicit constants, or demonstrating that the ratio tends to a constant depending on $p$ and $\varepsilon$, possibly with logarithmic corrections. Formal conditions: for fixed $\varepsilon>0$ and $p>0$, determine limits such as $\lim_{n\to\infty} T_{\rm CG}/T_{\rm RCD}$ or $\lim_{n\to\infty} T_{\rm CG}/n^{\alpha}$ for some $\alpha$, and identify the exact constants.

literature.title: Kaniel (1966) - Estimates for some computational techniques in linear algebra
literature.description: Provides early convergence bounds for the conjugate gradient method based on the spectral distribution, which are foundational for analyzing iteration counts on matrices with given eigenvalue decay.

literature.title: Golub and Van Loan (1996) - Matrix Computations
literature.description: Contains standard analysis of CG convergence and the role of condition number and eigenvalue clustering, providing background for comparing with randomized methods.

literature.title: Greenbaum (1997) - Iterative Methods for Solving Linear Systems
literature.description: Discusses the convergence behavior of CG and related methods, including how eigenvalue distribution affects iteration counts, which is directly relevant to the problem's spectral setting.

literature.title: Saad (2003) - Iterative Methods for Sparse Linear Systems
literature.description: Covers convergence theory for Krylov subspace methods including CG, and discusses the influence of eigenvalue distribution on iteration counts.

literature.title: Drineas, Kannan, Mahoney (2006) - Fast Monte Carlo Algorithms for Matrices I
literature.description: Introduces randomized algorithms for linear algebra that can be compared to deterministic Krylov methods, though not specifically CG versus RCD.

literature.title: Rokhlin and Tygert (2008) - A fast randomized algorithm for overdetermined linear least-squares regression
literature.description: Discusses randomized algorithms for least squares that can be contrasted with deterministic iterative methods, relevant to the RCD approach.

literature.title: Avron, Maymounkov, Toledo (2010) - Blendenpik: Supercharging LAPACK's least-squares solver
literature.description: Presents a randomized preconditioned least-squares solver, showing practical performance comparisons between randomized and deterministic iterative methods.

literature.title: Golub and Meurant (2010) - Matrices, Moments and Quadrature with Applications
literature.description: Provides detailed analysis of CG convergence using quadrature and spectral information, which can be applied to the power-law spectrum in the problem.
